To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
VEGF induces lymphangiogenesis during late-stage lung development.

a modest, physiologically relevant increase in VEGF-A in distal lung in the perinational period disrupts normal development of the gas exchange units by disrupting the established blood vessel network, increasing endothelial cell number and altering endothelial cell ultrastructure, and causes a three-fold increase in small lymphatic vessels.
a pathologically relevant increase of VEGF in the perinatally developing lung disrupts the established vascular network and increases lymphatic vessels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the basic mechanisms of late stage lung development, which will provide a foundation for understanding and improving lung development in the preterm infant.
understanding how the developing lung vascular system is regulated during the late stages of lung development.
understanding how VEGF signaling influences vascular development during lung organogenesis and how this process can go awry leading to vascular abnormalities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data presented herein show that VEGF induces lymphangiogenesis during lung organogenesis, and that the timing and magnitude of VEGF induction is crucial to the final outcome of vascular patterning.
VEGF induces lymphangiogenesis in late stage fetal lung development.
VEGF-induced lymphatic hyperplasia in the late stage of lung development is associated with impaired alveologenesis and mesenchymal cell death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VEGF-A pathway has a role in lymphatic development and that the balance of VEGF isoforms and receptors is critical for normal lung development.
VEGF is a key regulator of vascular development and that the response to VEGF is context dependent.

a modest increase in VEGF-A during a critical period of lung development leads to a significant disruption of vascular and alveolar development and a significant increase in the lymphatic vascular network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VEGF plays a key role in the development of the lymphatics in lung.
VEGF is a critical player in the formation of the lung vascular network.
VEGF is a key regulator of the developing lung vasculature.
